method: ESPN publishes no college depth charts, so the order here is usage: each team's quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends (positions from ESPN's roster) ranked by their projected share of the team's passes, carries or catches, a decayed average of this season. Yards and catches are the college model's projections per game, touchdowns the season average. College box scores carry no snap counts, so usage is a share of touches, not snaps. These are projections, not picks. Backtest on 2026 weeks 7 to 9, tuned on weeks 4 to 6, each game projected only from the games before it: Usage share (points), average miss 9.2 vs 10.1 season average and 9.6 last 3 (better than both; by squared error 15.2 vs 16.1, better, 4,579 games); Passing yards, average miss 67.0 vs 68.6 season average and 73.2 last 3 (better than both, 331 games); Rushing yards, average miss 29.1 vs 30.3 season average and 31.3 last 3 (better than both, 948 games); Receptions, average miss 1.44 vs 1.45 season average and 1.51 last 3 (better than both, 1,768 games); Receiving yards, average miss 22.7 vs 22.8 season average and 23.8 last 3 (level with the better one, 1,768 games); Touchdowns, average miss 0.502 vs 0.502 season average and 0.498 last 3 (worse than the last 3; by squared error 0.7 vs 0.7, level, 2,023 games).

backtest.window: 2026 weeks 7 to 9, tuned on weeks 4 to 6
